headline: Sent the Landscape Standards Ordinance to council after changes; tabled the social services funding agreement and license plate reader rules.
summary: Jessica Muise presented the Public Art Master Plan, and the committee discussed changes made since its last meeting. Veterans Committee membership changes adding American Legion and AMVETS members were sent to council, 5-0.
decisions: Approved setting the land-area minimum to 15% for all five items in the Landscape Standards Ordinance, 3-2.
Approved removing the planting list reference from Subsection F.1 of the Landscape Standards Ordinance, 5-0.
Approved adding “Any new or existing” to Subsection H.f. of the Landscape Standards Ordinance, 5-0.
Sent the Landscape Standards Ordinance to council, 5-0.
Tabled the Use of License Plate Readers/Surveillance Technology item for review by departments that already have policies, 4-1.
Approved Norman Belanger's amendment adding Post 1 AMVETS to the Veterans Committee membership change, 5-0.
Sent the amended Veterans Committee membership change to council, 5-0.
Tabled the Cooperating Agreement for Social Services Funding, 3-2.

plain_text:
City of Biddeford 
Policy Committee 
September 28, 2026 at 6:00 PM 
City Hall Council Chambers & Teams 
1. Roll Call Council President Beaupre, Councilor Jake Pierson, Marie Potvin, Norman 
Belanger, Remote- Councilor Kurtz   Time: 6:01 
2. Pledge of Allegiance 
3. Adjustment(s) to Agenda- None  
4. Approval of Minutes  
4.a Policy Committee Minutes 20260824 
Motion to approve the minutes by Councilor Pierson 
Second by Norman Belanger  
Passed Vote: 4-0 Councilor Kurtz lost connection 
5. Discussion/Review 
5.a Public Art Commission -Public Art Master Plan- Jessica Muise presented the Public Art 
Master Plan and discussed the changes made since the last meeting  
5.b Proposed Landscape Standards Ordinance- 
Motion to accept Norman Belanger  
Second by Councilor Pierson  
Using language in the landscape and nursery trade. Comments Section E Landscaping 
plan required question about no requirement for single or two family dwellings? Max noted 
that the threshold was anything that required planning board or site plan review -not meant 
to be a burden to homeowners, especially small property owners. There are a lot of people 
who may own homes on fixed incomes. Other communities have set strict standards on 
plantings and he personally didn’t feel it was appropriate. Shoreland Overlay Zones are 
already required by code for certain standards.  
Section F minimum – percentages of total land area. Understand the rationale as to why 
those numbers are less than the others. That table was done by Brad Favreau. The 
minimum went to the use vs. the lot. Modeled these requirements after the Scarborough
ordinance but tweaked it to fit Biddeford’s urban environment. Require more for softer 
uses than commercial and industrial. He would like to see all the numbers be at 15%.   
Motion by  Councilor Pierson to amend Subsection F. 1. modify the chart 15% for all 5 
items total land area. This makes it simpler for staff to track. Mixed use vs. development 
and creates extra steps etc. if it’s all the same there isn’t incentive to “cheat the system” 
Second Council President Beaupre 
As you deliberate, Industrial and Manufacturing uses having the lower percentages 10% for 
FMI would equate to a similar number as the smaller lots for 15%. Mixed used is probably 
the same in terms of lot size.  
Councilor Kurtz asked a procedural question- is substantive change to the underlying 
ordinance allowed in Policy? Answer was yes.  
Norman Belanger noted that he does not support the amendment as he doesn’t want to be 
overly aggressive. 
Vote: 3- 2 Motion passes 
 Councilor Pierson, Councilor Kurtz and Marie Potvin in favor 
Councilor Beaupre and Norman Belanger opposed  
Motion by Councilor Pierson  to amend Subsection F.1. To delete the “adhere to the 
preferred planting list to the UME”. Delete the whole line as follows “Species planted in 
accordance with this ordinance should adhere to the preferred planting list maintained by 
the University of Maine Cooperative Extension.”  It’s not something that’s kept updated 
and we would pigeonhole ourselves to a list that is not updated. You are covering yourself 
by using a landscape architect.   
Second by Norman Belanger 
Vote unanimous: 5-0 motion passes  
Subsection F.6.  
This needs a little more teeth to this in the sense of having some ways you can protect 
trees and they could have been damaged by construction that you cannot see. Some 
language to allow for the retention. Not a heavy lift for the staff. What does protection 
mean during construction. Section H there was a line for plantings that die to be replaced 
in perpetuity –
Motion by Councilor Pierson to amend Subsection H. f.  to add language  “ Any new or 
existing” landscaping” 
Second by Norman Belanger   
Public comment about replacing a 50 YO tree 
Vote Unanimous: 5-0 Motion passed 
Final vote  
Vote Unanimous: 5-0 Motion passed to send to council.  
Marie Potvin asked about enforcement. Max pointed out Section J item 1. 125% of the cost 
of landscaping held in escrow for 3 years after the three-year period there is a section that 
requires it to be maintained in perpetuity. It’s really an enforcement issue. Up to residents 
to bring complaints to city staff of developers aren’t doing their due diligence. Staff can 
enforce when noticed when doing inspections or other site walks. That language is already 
in the code.  
Norman Belanger asked if the 125% is just right. Their performance bonds are 110%. 
However, Max feels the 125% is appropriate and its only for the landscaping portion. It’s a 
smaller chunk of the expenses.  
5.c Use of License Plate Readers/Surveillance Technology -Biddeford 
Motion to consider Councilor Pierson 
Second for discussion Norman Belanger  
 
Discussion- Norman Belanger noted  he read the ordinance a couple of times and found it 
hard to understand. Noted the purpose and the requirements but no clear delineations. It 
is far too complicated a solution for them to be adopting in Biddeford and if it is adopted it 
needs further clarification 
Councilor Pierson  concurred that it is verbose we are in a time period where this is an 
important discussion to be had and to be clear about what we are/ aren’t doing for data 
collection.  Difficult to achieve at the local level. It would behoove us to use this as a 
starting point to talk with the team – City solicitor and PD to see what we are aren’t doing 
and have a better gauge of where we see a potential problem down the road. We don’t 
have a lot of data.  
Council President Beaupre – read it several times as well. It’s going beyond the ALPR 
designation of what we are trying to achieve. Cameras for activities and there are also
devices used by PD to monitor traffic incidences. Discussion has come up with body 
cams. There are already policies in place for the school dept. How long are the retention 
policies for the PD and other agencies with the city it’s not shared unless it needs to be 
reviewed. Has difficulty with the specificity and it may conflict with CALEA and conflicts 
with School Committee policies and recording of students and their activities.  
Motion by Council President Beaupre to Table for further review by departments  that 
already have policies to review   
Second by Councilor Pierson  
Motion Passed: 4-1 Councilor Pierson, Councilor Beupre, Marie Potvin and Norman 
Belanger in the affirmative; Councilor Kurtz in the negative 
 
5.d Veterans Committee Membership- 
Motion by Councilor Pierson to amend the current ordinance the change presented 
Second Marie Potvin  
Approve the change to the Veterans Committee to add representatives of the AmVets and 
American legion housed within Biddeford. To help establish a quorum.  
Norman Belanger Motion to amend by adding “and Post 1 AMVETS” after American Legion  
“hereby created and established the Veterans Committee, comprised of seven members, 
which shall include an active member of Post 26 of the American Legion, an active 
member of Post 1 of AMVETS, and a staff member of the General Assistance Office serving 
in an ex- officio capacity. With the exception of the representatives from the American 
Legion and Post 1 AMVETS, all other voting members shall be honorably discharged armed 
forces veterans, US citizens, and reside within the corporate limits of the City of 
Biddeford.” 
Second by Councilor Beauore 
Councilor Pierson  
Vote Unanimous in favor: 5-0  
Final Vote as amended to send to council  
Councilor Kurtz asked a question about membership of committees  
Vote Unanimous in favor: 5-0
5.e Cooperating Agreement for Social Services Funding- 
Motion by Councilor Pierson to adopt to move to Council  
Second by Norman Belanger  
Councilor Kurtz noted he would be more comfortable if this didn’t originate by Policy but 
rather by Council discussion.  
Councilor Kurtz made a motion to table the matter 
Second by Norman Belanger  
Vote 3-2 to be tabled Norman Belanger, Councilor Kurtz, Marie Potvin tabled to council for 
further discussion. Councilor Beaupre and Councilor Pierson in the negative. 
5.f Rules of the Council- Discussion 
Under city charter direction for rules of the council to be in place. Withing the rules 
Appendix is committees and should be placed under administration. Placed with other 
committees and then provision within the rules of the Council that they are a policy 
decision 2/3 votes and become effective immediately vs. a rule going to policy and two 
readings of city council.  
Norman Belanger noted the charter says they can adopt rules of procedure. That’s just 
where they place them. They shouldn’t be subject to emergency rules and can be waived 
by the council – you can’t waive provisions of an ordinance.  Move committees to the 
boards, commissions, committees.  
6. Other Business  
7.Adjourn  
Motion to adjourn Norman Belanger  
Second by Marie Potvin  
Vote Unanimous. 5-0 Meeting adjourned at 7:09pm
